findings.evidenceJa: まともに頭が働くじゃない、貴方
findings.governingReading: Rin dryly notes that Shirou’s head is functioning normally after all.
findings.explanation: The English turns a backhanded observation about present functioning into straightforward praise of intelligence.

findings.evidenceJa: 自分でぶっ飛んだ中身をどうにかしたのよ
findings.governingReading: Shirou himself somehow dealt with the insides that had been blown out.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the grotesque observed damage with generic wounds, weakening what makes the recovery extraordinary.

findings.highlight: if that’s the case, I’ve nothing to worry about.
findings.evidenceJa: そうだったらわたしが悩む必要はなかったっていう事よ。
findings.governingReading: Rin means that if Shirou had already learned such healing, she would not have needed to puzzle over the cause.
findings.explanation: The English makes the counterfactual a present reassurance and reverses her statement from prior diagnostic uncertainty to absence of concern.

findings.highlight: optimistic hopes that you’ll survive any major wounds.
findings.evidenceJa: 多少の傷なら治る、なんていう甘い考え
findings.governingReading: He must abandon the complacent idea that modest wounds will simply heal.
findings.explanation: The English changes “some/minor wounds” to major wounds, narrowing Rin’s warning to catastrophic injury.

findings.highlight: taking damage and having Saber helping me.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺がかってにケガして、それでセイバーから何かを貰ってる
findings.governingReading: Shirou feels guilty about getting himself hurt on his own initiative and thereby taking something from Saber.
findings.explanation: The English removes his agency and turns an involuntary drain or transfer into Saber intentionally helping.

findings.highlight: I won’t allow myself to be wrong!
findings.evidenceJa: そうでなければ許さないんだから、とくにわたしが！
findings.governingReading: If Magecraft did not consume money, Rin personally would never forgive it.
findings.explanation: The English changes her comic financial grievance into refusal to admit an incorrect claim.

findings.highlight: I haven’t made my mind up yet.
findings.evidenceJa: ただ考えがおよばないだけ。
findings.governingReading: It is not reluctance to answer; his thinking simply has not reached that far.
findings.explanation: The English says he is consciously undecided, giving him a developed choice he has not yet conceived.

findings.highlight: I’m not too sure about risking my life
findings.evidenceJa: 命を張るのは、どうかと思う
findings.governingReading: He judges staking his life for something unwanted to be objectionable or dubious.
findings.explanation: “Not too sure” weakens an ethical/practical judgment into uncertainty.

findings.highlight: the Servants try to eliminate other Servants even without orders from their Masters.
findings.evidenceJa: サーヴァントはマスターが命令しなくとも他のマスターを消しにかかる。
findings.governingReading: Servants may move to eliminate other Masters without being ordered by their own Masters.
findings.explanation: The English changes the targets from Masters to Servants, contradicting the following explanation about neutralizing Masters.

findings.highlight: Heroic spirits are a phenomenon. They can’t be killed.
findings.evidenceJa: 英霊っていうのはもう死んでも死なない現象だからね。
findings.governingReading: Heroic Spirits are a phenomenon for which dying no longer results in permanent death.
findings.explanation: The English first discusses Servants being eliminated, then categorically says they cannot be killed, erasing the temporary-death distinction at issue.

findings.evidenceJa: 人の姿をしたモノが息絶える
findings.governingReading: A being in human form ceases breathing in this world even if the death is temporary.
findings.explanation: Disappearance euphemizes the death-like bodily event that grounds Shirou’s moral objection.

findings.highlight: But stillI’m not strong enough to judge people’s deaths as good or bad.
findings.evidenceJa: それでも俺は人の生き死にに善悪を計れるほど強くはない。
findings.governingReading: Shirou says he is not strong enough to weigh good and evil in whether people live or die.
findings.explanation: The missing space visibly fuses the turn at the center of his ethical self-assessment.

findings.evidenceJa: 相手を殺すための戦い
findings.governingReading: Shirou refuses a fight undertaken for the purpose of killing the opponent.
findings.explanation: “Fight to the death” can include unavoidable mortal danger and obscures the purposive killing he rejects while still allowing self-defense.

findings.highlight: Humans can’t see those in spirit form.
findings.evidenceJa: 霊感のない人間には姿さえ観測できない。
findings.governingReading: Humans without spiritual perception cannot even observe a Servant in spirit form.
findings.explanation: The English makes all humans categorically unable to see them and deletes the stated perception qualifier.

findings.highlight: is like a natural death for normal people.
findings.evidenceJa: 一般人から見れば自然災害のようなものなのだ。
findings.governingReading: To ordinary people, killing by a Servant appears like a natural disaster.
findings.explanation: Natural death is a different causal category and breaks the comparison to invisible, uncontrollable calamity.

findings.evidenceJa: サーヴァントいや、マスターとサーヴァントは
findings.governingReading: Shirou begins with Servants, corrects himself, and says Masters and Servants.
findings.explanation: The missing punctuation and spacing fuse “Servants” and “no,” damaging an audible self-correction.

findings.evidenceJa: 魔術を連発できるって事だろ
findings.governingReading: Shirou checks whether greater reserves mean repeated use of magical power or techniques.
findings.explanation: In context the energy enables Servants’ own abilities; generic “magic” risks recasting those abilities as ordinary spellcasting.

findings.highlight: the magical energy of their Master.
findings.evidenceJa: 主であるマスターの魔力分しか生前の力を発揮できないの
findings.governingReading: A Servant can manifest its living-era power only within its own energy plus what its Master supplies.
findings.explanation: The English leaves Rin’s quoted explanation typographically unclosed at the page boundary.

findings.governingReading: Rin retracts her generalization because many became heroes precisely through tyranny or violent domination.
